Consider the picture below. Given that $\mathbf{m}=\lambda\mathbf{n}+\mu\mathbf{k}$, find $\lambda$ and $\mu$.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/b8abf22d14f93a38c4d01f368b8171e4ccfe90086d932f5b58453baa46391405.png)
e-4287.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/76b9867a7c1ef484922241ebe44272f0104e406c31310bf36227a13850f50d8b.png)

In $\bigtriangleup ONM$ shown above, we have:

- $ON=2|\mathbf{n}|$;

- $\overrightarrow{ON}$ and $\mathbf{n}$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overrightarrow{ON}=2\mathbf{n}$.

Similarly:

- $NM=2|\mathbf{k}|$

- $\overrightarrow{NM}$ and $\mathbf{k}$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overrightarrow{NM}=2\mathbf{k}$.

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\overset{\to }{ON}+\overset{\to }{NM} \\  & =2n+2k.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $\mathbf{m}=\lambda\mathbf{n}+\mu\mathbf{k}=2\mathbf{n}+2\mathbf{k}$. 

Since $\mathbf{n} \nparallel \mathbf{k},$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $\mathbf{n}$ and $\mathbf{k}$, we get:

- $\lambda=2$ and $\mu=2$

decision.explanation: The grid gives j=(-2,-4), k=(4,0), and l=(-6,4). Vertical components give λ=-1; then 2+4μ=-6 gives μ=-2. Thus l=-j-2k.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/6c9273c0b89d4c06c8a8591b8e8e94b0c83b2d1d4bd04b64ed8cb0a185619b5f.png)

In $△OJL$ shown above, we have 

- $OJ=|j|$

- $\overset{\to }{OJ}$ has the opposite direction to $j$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OJ}=-j.$

Similarly:

- $JL=2|k|$

- $\overset{\to }{JL}$ has the opposite direction to $k$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{JL}=-2k.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}l & =\overset{\to }{OJ}+\overset{\to }{JL} \\  & =-j-2k.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $l=\lambda j+\mu k=-j-2k.$

Since $j∦k,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =-1$ and $\mu =-2$
